look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: find stiff, sharply angled green stems that appear almost leafless; inspect the nodes for clusters of tiny separate male or female flowers. Confirm minute alternate scale-like upper leaves and reddish fringed stipules rather than assuming the green shoots are grass blades.

project_inclusion.notes: Australian native, not a confirmed Hays/target-zone native. Included solely because learner source-pool admission is independent of native-range certification.

taxonomy_notes: Accepted species under the Australian Plant Census and VicFlora; Leptomeria xiphoclada is a synonym. Several varieties occur in Australia; source-pool species-level concept is not an extra card for a variety.

morphology_keys.habit: Erect broomlike subshrub about 20–90 cm tall; stems rigid, smooth and angular, sometimes nearly leafless.
morphology_keys.leaves_attachment: Leaves alternate and sessile when present; lower leaves small (about 5–15 mm), often toothed; upper leaves narrow or scale-like. Look at a stem node for reddish-brown fringed stipules.
morphology_keys.flower_reproductive: Small flowers clustered at nodes, usually male and female on separate plants (dioecious). Male flowers have a 4–5-lobed calyx and 6–9 free stamens; female flowers have a 5-lobed calyx and short styles. Do not label sex of the photographed cluster without a closer verified view.
morphology_keys.fruit_seed: Small 2–4 mm capsule; glossy dark ovoid seeds about 1.5–2.5 mm, with roughened surface.

confused_with: Juncus spp. (rushes; superficial grasslike green shoots)
Ephedra spp. (green jointed stems, different reproductive structures)
leaf-reduced Euphorbiaceae (family-level resemblance, not a local Amperea species)
comparisons.key_distinctions: Rushes carry grasslike flowers/fruit rather than small Euphorbiaceae flowers clustered along angular woody stems. Ephedra has opposite/whorled scale leaves and seed-bearing cones, not Amperea's alternate small leaves, fringed stipules and capsules. These are shape comparisons only: Amperea is Australian and not a local encounter claim.
